newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem, Ben Ali see Mercosur-Maghreb trade growth.
newsitem.headline: Menem, Ben Ali see Mercosur-Maghreb trade growth.

text.p: Presidents Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali of Tunisia and Carlos Menem of Argentina held private talks here on Wednesday and agreed there were "excellent prospects" for trade between their regional groupings, officials said.
Ben Ali and Menem talked for an hour with senior aides from both countries then lunched in private on the last day of Ben Ali's three-day visit.
Argentina is a member of South America's Mercosur customs union with Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay. Tunisia is one of the North African countries in the Maghreb grouping.

Menem said at a dinner in Ben Ali's honour on Tuesday night that there was a need to "promote greater participation of the private sectors and businessmen" in bilateral relations. They also discussed the Middle East peace process.

The two countries signed accords on cooperation on the environment, animal health, farming and economic, cultural and educational cooperation. But the real impetus to the visit was to boost trade in energy, agriculture, tourism and shipping.
Two-way trade between Tunisia and Argentina grew to $108 million in 1996 from $28 million a year earlier.
Menem has visited Tunisia twice but this was Ben Ali's first trip to Argentina.
